extracted.intended_audience: prospective Searle Scholars applicants and host institution administrators (research faculty and grants officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Program-level rules and recipient obligations for Searle Scholars awards, including award amount and payment schedule, eligible recipient institution type, reporting and meeting attendance requirements, acknowledgement language, and nondiscrimination policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and payment schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are set at $450,000 for a three-year period with $150,000 payable in the first year and equal sums payable in the second and third years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments for years 2 and 3 are subject to the receipt of acceptable progress reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical number and activation date of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the program grants 15 new awards annually, activated on July 1 of the year of the competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informational—indicates typical cohort size and award start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient institution tax-status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards are made to tax-exempt institutions described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award is paid to the institution (not directly to the individual); applicants should ensure host institution meets 501(c)(3) status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of award funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are designated for the support of the research described in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds must be used to support the research project as proposed in the application; deviations may be subject to program review/approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report condition for continued payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments for subsequent years are subject to the receipt of acceptable progress reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must submit acceptable progress reports on schedule to receive year 2 and year 3 payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting attendance and scientific report
rubrics_metrics.description: Searle Scholars are expected to attend the Annual Searle Scholars Meeting, normally held in Chicago in April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific reports, consisting of an abstract and headshot, are requested prior to the annual meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual and final fiscal/scientific reporting deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarded institution shall submit an annual fiscal report each year of the award; these reports are requested in July and due in August. Final scientific and fiscal reports will be due within 60 days of termination of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should calendar these dates (annual request in July, due in August; final reports within 60 days after award end) to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of support in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any publication arising from work supported by the Program should be acknowledged as having received funds from the 'Searle Scholars Program.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified acknowledgement wording in any resulting publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination policy applicable to selection
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the policy of the Searle Scholars Program to operate without discrimination as to age, race, religion, sex, disability, or national origin in the employment or promotion of staff. This policy will be applied to the selection of the Searle Scholars as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and program operations follow nondiscrimination principles; applicants and institutions should note this commitment.
